mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES keeps rising from its recent trough, commuting-linked trips will continue to normalize and spill into nearby retail and restaurants, pushing RETAIL_REC above the last four-week mean within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -45.1 to -36.1 while TRANSIT improved from -58.7 to -48.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average over the next 28 days even as WORKPLACES rises for at least two consecutive weeks and TRANSIT does not deteriorate further.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls back toward baseline, people are spending less time at home and more time out for discretionary errands, which raises retail visits within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below 12 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 18.6 to 13.7 across the snapshot while RETAIL_REC stayed deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last four weeks within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL falls below 12 points above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current level signals tighter access or weaker city-center circulation, which suppresses retail foot traffic and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from the current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains very depressed at -48.4 and has not recovered to within 40 points of baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its previous four-week mean despite a further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Retail demand will recover only if WORKPLACES improves while TRANSIT improves at the same time; the joint return of office attendance and station use increases weekday shopping visits more than either series alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both work and transit remain far below baseline but have been trending upward over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform its prior four-week average over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility keeps falling, outdoor substitution into leisure districts weakens and some discretionary trips shift back toward indoor retail destinations, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 points and stays there for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -4.9 to -14.3 across the snapshot, a sharp drop in outdoor activity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 to 14 days after PARKS drops below -15 points and remains below that level for a full week.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM means fewer essential trips and less general out-of-home errand intensity, which will also pull down discretionary retail over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -16.0 to -11.4 while retail remained near -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last four-week mean over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying flat or declining from the current level.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in TRANSIT paired with a recovery in WORKPLACES will restore weekday congregation patterns; if only one improves, retail will not rebound materially, but if both improve together retail will rise within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise by at least 3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved over the snapshot but remain deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move above its prior four-week average within 28 days after TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise by at least 3 points in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable reopening regime, a sustained reduction in RESIDENTIAL time combined with a smaller decline in PARKS indicates more time spent away from home in mixed-use settings, which should raise RETAIL_REC within two to four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from 18.6 to 13.7 while PARKS stayed near baseline but turned more negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its previous four-week average even as RESIDENTIAL declines further and PARKS stops falling or stabilizes for two consecutive weeks.
